samples.summary: `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all clears `selectedImage` on the *modifier* keydown that precedes Cmd/Ctrl+C, so the #870 fix never fires on a real keyboard
samples.evidence: `handleKeyDown` (text-editor.ts:864) hands EVERY keydown to `imageKeyHandler`, including the keydown for the modifier key itself. Pressing Cmd/Ctrl produces a keydown with `e.key === 'Meta'` / `'Control'` *before* the `c` keydown. In `imageKeyHandler` that event has `key === 'Meta'`, which matches neither the new `mod && (key==='c'||key==='x')` branch (line 2341) nor Escape/Delete/Arrow, so it falls into the catch-all at 2385-2386: `selectedImage = null; return false;`. By the time the `c` keydown arrives, `selectedImage` is already null, `imageKeyHandler` returns false at line 2321, and `imageSelectionProvider` (2287-2288) returns null — so `handleCopy`'s new image branch (text-editor.ts:1210-1211) writes nothing. Same for Cmd/Ctrl+X. The new tests never dispatch the modifier-only keydown (they synthesize a single `keydown` with `metaKey: true`), so they cannot see this. Net effect: the shortcut this change exists to fix still copies nothing in a browser; only the programmatic/context-menu path works.

samples.summary: The catch-all clears `selectedImage` without re-rendering, leaving the image selection overlay painted while the state is gone
samples.evidence: Lines 2385-2386 do `selectedImage = null; return false;` with no `render()` call, unlike every other clearing branch in the same handler (Escape at 2349, Arrow at 2371/2380, `imageSelectionClearer` at 2306). For a key the text path does nothing with (e.g. a bare `Shift`, `Alt`, `Meta`, `F5`, `CapsLock`), no render is triggered afterwards, so the selection handles/overlay stay drawn on a selection that no longer exists — a subsequent click on a handle then reads `selectedImage` as null and behaves inconsistently with what the user sees.

samples.summary: `imageSelectionClearer` is wired only into `handleCut`'s text path; the other selection-deleting paths that shift the same offsets do not call it
samples.evidence: The new field's doc comment (text-editor.ts:286-293) states the invariant: any path that deletes a text selection shifts the offsets the image selection is expressed in, so the image selection must be dropped. Only `handleCut` (line 1259) honours it. `deleteSelection()` is also called from `handlePaste`'s insert path (line 1348), `insertText` (819), `handleInput` (641/706), and the find/replace paths (5506, 5519). Keyboard-driven variants are incidentally covered because `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all clears on the keydown, but the API-driven ones are not: `editor.paste()` (editor.ts:3386) and replace-all are invoked from React UI with no keydown on the textarea, so a coexisting image selection survives at an offset that now names a different inline — exactly the mis-targeted Delete the new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:766 documents as the harm.

samples.summary: Sibling image-selection API entry points still use the throwing `doc.getBlock` with a dead `if (!block)` guard, the exact hazard the new provider guards against
samples.evidence: `imageSelectionProvider` (2289-2294) deliberately switched to `doc.findBlock` because `Doc.getBlock` throws (`document.ts:187: throw new Error('Block not found')`). The neighbouring API methods were not updated: `selectImageAt` (3682), `getSelectedImage` (3695) and `updateSelectedImage` (3708) all call `doc.getBlock(...)` followed by `if (!block) return`, which is unreachable — a stale `selectedImage` after a remote peer deletes the block makes these throw instead of returning null. This change makes stale image selections longer-lived (Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+X now deliberately keep the selection alive rather than clearing it), widening the window in which those methods can throw.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `text-editor.ts:848-866` routes every keydown (only IME-composition at 851 and `pasting` at 854 return early; no modifier filter exists anywhere in packages/docs/src/view) into `imageKeyHandler`. In `editor.ts:2320-2387`, a modifier-only keydown has `e.key === 'Meta'`/`'Control'`, which after normalization at 2327 matches neither the copy/cut branch (2341, requires key 'c'/'x'), nor Escape (2344), Delete/Backspace (2352), nor the arrows (2362-2364) — so it reaches the catch-all at 2385-2386 which sets `selectedImage = null`. Because the Meta/Control keydown physically precedes the 'c'/'x' keydown in a real browser, `selectedImage` is already null when the copy shortcut arrives: `imageKeyHandler` bails at 2321, `imageSelectionProvider` returns null at 2288, and `handleCopy`/`handleCut` return without writing at text-editor.ts:1210-1211 and 1249-1250. The keyboard path this change exists to fix therefore copies/cuts nothing; only the programmatic/context-menu path works. No guard makes this unreachable and it is squarely a logic/ordering correctness bug on a normal-use path.

searchedFor: grep focus() in text-editor.ts and editor.ts
finding.summary: Clicking an image never focuses the hidden textarea, so the new Cmd/Ctrl+C image-copy path can't fire when focus is elsewhere (notably read-only docs)
finding.evidence: The image hit branch of `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2502-2511) calls `e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` and sets `selectedImage`, but never calls `textEditor.focus()`. It is registered with `{capture: true}` (editor.ts:2522), so `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` — the only place that calls `this.focus()` (text-editor.ts:1673) — never runs for an image click. All the new plumbing (`imageKeyHandler`, `handleCopy`/`handleCut` image branches) is attached to the hidden textarea (text-editor.ts:560-565), so it only receives keydown/copy/cut when that textarea already has focus. In read-only mode the editor deliberately does NOT focus on mount (editor.ts:2757: `if (!readOnly) textEditor.focus();` with the comment that focus is 'acquired on first click … via handleMouseDown'), so a viewer whose first click is on an image gets no focus, no `copy` event, and issue #870 persists exactly as before. The same holds in edit mode whenever focus has moved to a toolbar/sidebar control before the image click.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the image-hit branch of handleImageMouseDown never focuses the hidden textarea. It does, via a helper. editor.ts:2544-2553 (the image body hit branch) calls selectImageInline(hit.blockId, hit.offset), and selectImageInline at editor.ts:1255-1259 does `selection.setRange(null); selectedImage = {...}; textEditorRef?.focus();`. The comment at editor.ts:1241-1254 explicitly documents this focus call as the fix for precisely the scenario described (capture-phase stopPropagation prevents TextEditor.handleMouseDown from focusing, and read-only never focuses on mount, so Cmd/Ctrl+C and the copy event would not reach the textarea). textEditorRef is assigned at editor.ts:2228 immediately after TextEditor construction, before any listener can fire, so the optional call is not a no-op. The read-only path is covered too: handleImageMouseDown early-returns when readOnly (editor.ts:2497), and the alternate selection entry point selectImageAt (editor.ts:3681-3687) also routes through selectImageInline and therefore focuses. The reviewer's cited line range 2502-2511 is the BUTTON/INPUT bail-out guard, not the image-hit branch, and their claim that text-editor.ts:1673 is the only focus() call is contradicted by editor.ts:1258.

mergedFrom.summary: `getSelectedImage` / `selectImageAt` / `updateSelectedImage` call the throwing `doc.getBlock`, so their `if (!block) return` guards are dead and a stale block id throws instead of returning null

finding.summary: `deleteSelectedImageInline` deletes 1 char at the stored image offset without re-validating the block/image, so a stale image selection either throws or deletes the wrong character
finding.evidence: editor.ts:2242-2252 does `const { blockId, offset } = selectedImage; docStore.snapshot(); doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1);` with no `doc.findBlock(blockId)` / `findImageAtOffset` check. Its sibling `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2256-2267) deliberately uses `findBlock` and re-checks `findImageAtOffset`, with a comment naming the exact hazard: "a block a remote peer just deleted". `MemDocStore.deleteText` -> `findBlockInAnyArray` throws `Block not found: <id>` (memory.ts:214-217, 331-353), so on that same remote-deletion scenario the Delete/Backspace route (`imageKeyHandler`, editor.ts:2309-2313) throws out of the keydown listener instead of returning null. If the block still exists but offsets shifted (remote insert before the image, or the text-selection cut path described in the next finding), the delete silently removes an unrelated character — data loss with an undo snapshot taken around it. This delta's new cut tests are the first coverage of the `imageDeleteHandler` wiring; the cut path happens to be guarded by the provider, the Delete path is not.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `deleteSelectedImageInline` calls `doc.deleteText({ blockId, offset }, 1)` on the stored selection "with no `doc.findBlock(blockId)` / `findImageAtOffset` check". Reading the function in the working tree (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2262-2283), it does exactly those checks: `const block = doc.findBlock(blockId); if (!block || !findImageAtOffset(block, offset)) { selectedImage = null; render(); return; }` — placed before `docStore.snapshot()` and `doc.deleteText`. `findImageAtOffset` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:457-467) returns null when the offset no longer names an image inline, so the remote-block-deletion case (would-be `Block not found` throw out of the keydown listener via imageKeyHandler at editor.ts:2352-2356) and the shifted-offset wrong-character-deletion case are both short-circuited, with the stale selection cleared. The guard is the same pair used by the sibling `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2287-2298). The repo's own task log (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:186-192) records this exact defect as already fixed in the same manner, consistent with the code. The code is not as described.

finding.summary: When a text selection and a click-selected image coexist, the text branch of `handleCut` deletes the text but never clears the parent's image selection, leaving `selectedImage` pointing at a shifted offset
finding.evidence: The new test at copy-integrity.test.ts:285-303 institutionalises the state where `selectedImage` and a text range are live at once (`selectImageAt` then `_setSelectionForTest`, asserting `getSelectedImage()` is still non-null after the copy). The cut counterpart is unguarded: `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1233-1253) takes the `hasSelection()` branch, calls `deleteSelection()`, and never touches `imageSelectionProvider`/`imageDeleteHandler`, so `selectedImage.offset` in editor.ts is left pointing into text that has moved. The render path (editor.ts:1853-1855) will then draw resize handles around whatever image now sits at that key, and a following Delete goes through the unvalidated `deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2242). The same stale state is produced by the copy branch, but only cut mutates the document.

verdict.reason: The finding claims handleCut's text branch deletes text without clearing the parent editor's image selection, leaving selectedImage at a shifted offset. The code is not as described. In packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts, handleCut's text path calls this.imageSelectionClearer?.() at line 1259 — immediately after e.preventDefault() (line 1256) and before both the table-cell branch (line 1261) and the block branch — with an explicit comment that the text path wins over a coexisting image selection and is about to move the text that selection's offset is measured against. The field is declared and documented for exactly this case at text-editor.ts:285-293, and it is wired by the parent at editor.ts:2303-2307, where it sets selectedImage = null and re-renders. Therefore no stale selectedImage survives a text cut, so the render path cannot draw handles around a shifted image and a following Delete cannot reach deleteSelectedImageInline with a stale offset. The finding's quoted range (1233-1253) stops three lines short of the clearing call. The copy branch's absence of a clear is intentional and non-mutating, which the finding itself concedes. Additionally, the cited test range copy-integrity.test.ts:285-303 contains afterEach teardown and the first table-cell copy test, not the described coexisting-selection test.
